title: Matlhowa (leg rattles)
summary: Matlhowa are leg or ankle rattles made from cocoons filled with pebbles or seeds, worn by dancers to add percussion to their own steps. Bands of the cocoon rattles are tied round the shins and sound with every stamp of the dancer.
howToPlay: Three places are lit on the band: Shake near the top, Stamp in the middle, Flick near the bottom.
The cocoons shiver and the pebbles inside them roll when a stroke sounds.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Keep the stamp on the beat.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The dancer plays the rattles with the feet: every stamp shakes the cocoons, so the dance makes its own music.
credits: Tradition: the matlhowa; patterns written for this game
